title: PRD: Holistic Inference SLA Simulator and Billing Validator
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:
This PRD describes a new product component: the Holistic Inference SLA Simulator and Billing Validator (referred to as "SLA Simulator"). The SLA Simulator is a configurable, deterministic simulation engine and UX that predicts production-level SLA outcomes and customer billing under proposed routing, fidelity, and capacity policies before they are deployed. It closes the gap between engineering experiments and commercial impacts by producing realistic, auditable forecasts that combine telemetry, routing logic, cost models, and capacity profiles.

Problem statement / Motivation:
- Operators and product managers lack a reproducible way to understand how routing and fidelity changes will affect customer SLOs, unit cost, and invoices without deploying risky experiments.
- Current offline experiments require bespoke scripts and expensive canaries; differences in traffic sampling, KV cache state, and multi-variant routing make post-hoc reconciliation inaccurate.
- Sales, finance, and customer success need a way to validate negotiated SLAs and proposed pricing changes against predicted violation and cost exposure prior to contracting.

Goals (must-have):
1) Simulate end-to-end request handling for a configurable tenant or traffic profile and output: predicted latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), expected token cost, and projected billing reconciliation deltas for a given period.
2) Incorporate real telemetry distributions (sequence length, prompt-prefix similarity, KV hit rates) as inputs, not static averages.
3) Validate SLO compliance for runbook actions (e.g., fallback to cheaper variant, regional failover) and compute the economic delta of each action.
4) Provide a Console scenario composer and API/CLI to run repeatable scenarios, save presets, and version results for audit.

Non-goals (out of scope):
- This PRD does not change runtime scheduling or routing logic itself; it only simulates the behavior of existing logic.
- It does not perform live traffic mirroring nor will it be used as a real-time decision engine in the first release.

User personas and primary user journeys:
- Product Manager: create a scenario for a planned variant rollout; compare projected p95 latency and monthly spend between baseline and new policy.
- SRE/Platform Engineer: validate a proposed autoscaling policy against SLA burn rates during a forecasted traffic surge.
- Sales/Finance: run a contract proposal validation to forecast penalty exposure and expected invoice for a customer-specific traffic profile.
- Solutions Engineer: reproduce a customer-reported incident in the simulator to validate root cause and remediation cost.

Functional requirements:
A. Inputs and ingestion:
  - Support ingestion of time-series telemetry snapshots (token per request distribution, sequence length histogram, KV cache hit-rate samples) as CSV/JSON or a pointer to an internal telemetry snapshot.
  - Accept model catalog cost inputs per-token and per-embedding for model variants and quantization levels.
  - Accept route/routing policy definitions (latency-tiered routing, region failover, affinity) with simple DSL or JSON.
  - Allow tenant-level overrides: per-route SLOs, committed capacity, and discounting rules.

B. Simulation engine (core):
  - Deterministically simulate single-request latency decomposition (network, runtime, kernel, queueing) using parametric models derived from historical profiling.
  - Model KV/prefix caching effects and warmup behavior using stateful session emulation across requests in a scenario run.
  - Model batching and its tradeoffs with latency and cost by simulating queueing/batcher behavior with configurable batch windows.
  - Produce per-interval (hourly/daily) estimates for service-level metrics and cost.

C. Outputs and artifacts:
  - Tabular report: predicted p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, and token-level cost per-route and per-tenant.
  - Billing delta report: projected invoice vs baseline including credits, overage exposure, and estimated SLA penalties.
  - Action explorer: estimated SLO-change and cost-change for alternative actions (enable prefetch, lower batch window, degrade quantization).
  - Audit log: deterministic input snapshot, engine version, and checksum to support reproducibility.

D. Interface and UX:
  - Console scenario composer with templates: "small-scale canary", "enterprise surge", "cross-region outage".
  - REST API and CLI to run scenarios, list presets, and retrieve reports in JSON/CSV.
  - Integration hook for the Console to show "simulate before rollout" on rollout pages.

E. Acceptance criteria and accuracy targets:
  - For a set of held-out customer scenarios, simulated p95 latency must be within +/- 12% of recorded production p95 for the same telemetry snapshot and routing policy.
  - Cost forecasts (per-tenant monthly) should be within +/- 8% of reconciled invoices for held-out historical windows.
  - Deterministic replay: repeating same scenario with same inputs and engine version must produce identical outputs and checksum.

Non-functional requirements:
- Response time: small scenarios (<= 100k simulated requests) must complete within 15 minutes in the alpha; large scenarios (<= 5M requests) must complete within 6 hours for GA.
- Security: simulator must honor confidentiality; internal tenant data used for scenarios must be accessible only to authorized roles and logged.
- Scalability: engine should scale horizontally to support parallel scenario runs; job queue must support prioritization and cancellation.
- Observability: publish execution metrics (wall time, simulated requests/sec, memory usage) into runtime-platform metrics and console.

SLOs for the product itself:
- Job scheduling/latency: 95% of queued scenario runs start within 2 minutes during normal load.
- Result availability: 99% of successfully completed runs have artifacts stored and downloadable.

Design constraints and assumptions:
- We rely on existing telemetry snapshot APIs; any changes to telemetry schema require simulator adapter changes.
- Cost model inputs are maintained by Finance and Billing teams; simulator will reference a versioned cost table.
- For accuracy, we assume the runtime performance profiles (kernel-level latency curves) are available from the serving-runtime profiling team.

High-level architecture (textual):
1) Ingestion layer: adapters that normalize telemetry snapshots and routing DSL into the internal scenario format.
2) Simulation core (stateless worker pods + stateful session store for multi-request emulation).
3) Cost & SLA evaluator: applies billing rules and SLO checks against simulation outputs.
4) Orchestration & persistence: job queue, artifact store (reports), and audit index.
5) Console / API: scenario composer, run manager, and results viewer.

Acceptance tests and validation plan:
- Create 10 representative historical scenarios (mix of enterprise and SMB tenants) and run the simulator; measure accuracy targets against historical telemetry.
- Canary: internal alpha with platform and SRE teams for 6 weeks; collect feedback on UX and model mismatches.
- Pilot: enable with 3 willing customers (Solutions + CSM) to validate contract forecasting with non-sensitive sanitized snapshots.

Rollout plan (milestones):
1) Alpha (Q2 2029): internal-only; API + CLI + basic console; small-scenario target; owners: product (Maya Chen), eng (owner: Runtime Sim Team), privacy (review).
2) Beta (Q3 2029): add cost-modeling hooks, preset library, and two customer pilots; financial reconciliation report.
3) GA (Q4 2029): scale to large scenarios, enforce RBAC, and surface "simulate before rollout" in the rollout UI.

Dependencies and cross-team commitments:
- Eng-serving-runtime: provide kernel latency curves and batching model parameters (owner: Priya Kapoor).
- Eng-platform/billing: maintain versioned cost tables and billing-rule sandbox (owner: Alex Martinez).
- Telemetry: provide snapshot API and data retention contracts.
- Security/Legal: define allowed sandboxing and anonymization patterns for customer snapshots.

Open questions and trade-offs:
- How much fidelity is necessary in kernel-level modeling vs. using black-box parametric latency functions? Trade-off: fidelity increases accuracy but adds maintenance cost.
- Should the simulator support live mirroring for ultra-high-fidelity comparison? This would increase risk and complexity.
- How to monetize the feature: part of Dedicate/Private add-on, or included in Optimize? Initial launch: internal and pilot; go-to-market decision later.

Metrics and success criteria post-GA:
- Adoption: number of scenario runs per month (target 1200 runs/month within 6 months).
- Impact: percentage reduction in SLA-regression rollouts (target 40% fewer incidents traced to rollout policy misconfig).
- Financial: reduction in unexpected SLA credits for customers in pilots (target reduce exposure by 35% for pilot customers).

Operational playbook (brief):
1) Failure modes: model drift in latency curves -> run scheduled recalibration job; inaccurate telemetry mapping -> adapter alerts.
2) Incident flow: if simulator reports > 20% delta vs production for the same snapshot, flag and create a task to reconcile inputs.
3) Support: triage channel #simulator-support; owners: Runtime Sim Team (oncall rotation) and Product.

Appendix A — Example CLI workflow:
# create scenario from telemetry snapshot
redwood-sim create --name "enterprise-surge-test" --snapshot s3://telemetry/tenantA/2029-01-12.json --policy-file ./policies/latency-tier.json --cost-table v2029-02-01
# run and wait
redwood-sim run --id <scenario-id> --wait --output ./reports/scenario-1234.json

Appendix B — Example routing DSL snippet (JSON input accepted):
{
  \"routes\": [
    {\"name\": \"primary\", \"variants\": [\"r1-small\", \"r1-medium\"], \"latency_target_ms\": 120},
    {\"name\": \"fallback\", \"variants\": [\"r2-quant\"], \"latency_target_ms\": 400}
  ],
  \"policy\": {\"batch_window_ms\": 20, \"kv_prefetch\": true}
}
(Adapters accept equivalent YAML/DSL.)

Appendix C — Acceptance checklist for Product Review:
- [ ] Ingestion adapters for the three primary telemetry formats implemented.
- [ ] Console scenario composer with 3 templates.
- [ ] API/CLI with JSON/CSV outputs and reproducible artifact checksums.
- [ ] Accuracy target met for the 10 validation scenarios.
- [ ] Pilot customers identified and NDA reviewed.

Owner and next steps:
Product owner: Maya Chen (product). Engineering lead: Daniel Ruiz (Runtime Sim Team). Target alpha kickoff: 2029-04-01. Next immediate task: finalize simulation parameter schema and prototype one end-to-end historical scenario within two sprints.
